findings.finding: All throwing caller/capture creation precedes final actor owner assignment and nonthrowing return. Facade stores that actual return before later validation.

Each original Auth attempt keeps its actual original parent and the immutable caller restriction. Temporary UI-operation attempts do not replace OriginalAuthRequestContext.parent, so a successful startup is not retired merely because that temporary view operation ends.
Auth forwarding and named auxiliary dispatch use original capture admissions; completion releases those admissions. No task cancellation is substituted for actual native completion.

Synchronous retirement stops future admissions. The retained close joins an already accepted Stop or calls original logout(false) before awaiting a retired startup. Historical close alone removes a retired parent restriction; unrelated Invocation binding is rejected.
A failing original Stop throws before retired-start join and before close receipt. The same registered caller and failed-close state remain retained. Only explicit retry admits another close attempt.
Without admitted startup or an actual Stop, close waits original caller/attempt operations and returns neverStartedDrained. No synthetic Stop success is created.

Only successful authentication-close receipt allows the facade to continue selection join, original FIFO frontier and consumer-task joins. releaseAfterRuntimeDrain independently refuses pending/failed auth close and does not claim those facade-specific facts.

limitations: This source review establishes compatibility and preserved ownership paths, not executed cancellation/Stop behavior. The full forwarded UI call sites, concrete composed framework compilation and real original native/SDK qualification remain separate gates.
